data.one_liner: Abstraction for the Segmented State Pattern to create custom state stores.
data.what_it_does: It provides a core architecture for separating state into three segments: state value, error, and loading status. Developers can build custom reactive stores on top of any reactivity system like Streams, ValueNotifier, or MobX.
use_when: You want to implement the Segmented State Pattern using custom reactivity.
You need built-in state history management with MementoMixin.
avoid_when: You prefer ready-made mainstream state management solutions without building custom stores.
You are looking for pre-built UI widget bindings directly inside the core library.
strengths: Flexibility to use any reactivity system as a basis.
Built-in support for middleware, executors, and tracking.
weaknesses: Requires manual boilerplate setup to implement reactive stores.
Documentation relies on external web links for deep dives.

alternatives.name: bloc
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you want a fully featured, production-ready state management library with built-in event handling instead of creating a custom store abstraction.

alternatives.name: riverpod
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you want compile-safe dependency injection and reactive state providers without managing store classes.
